> 勇於敢則殺，勇於不敢則活.

This chapter is built on a distinction that modern Chinese has collapsed: 勇 and 敢 are used as one word, and in 說文 they are two different things.

勇，氣也 — 勇 is a charge of energy, a breath of force.
敢，進取也 — 敢 is advancing to take.

勇 has no direction. 敢 supplies the direction.

## One charge of energy, two uses

A charge that goes out: 勇於敢.
The same charge held: 勇於不敢.

Both use the same 氣, and the force required to hold it is not less than the force required to release it.

Once that is clear, 不敢 stops being cowardice. It is not the absence of the charge — the charge is there, and it is not being carried forward to take something.

## 此兩者，或利或害

Both of these — one benefits, one harms.

The chapter does not say which is which in general. It says the two are not distinguishable from the outside, which is why the next question is about heaven.

## 天之所惡，孰知其故

What heaven dislikes — who knows the reason?

The line is unusually modest. The chapter is declining to give a rule, and that modesty is the argument: a rule is what 敢 wants.

## 是以聖人猶難之

The sage still treats it as hard.

猶 — still. Even with the distinction clear, he does not resolve it into a policy.

## 天之道：不爭而善勝，不言而善應，不召而自來

Not contending, and good at prevailing. Not speaking, and good at answering. Not summoning, and it arrives.

Three 不's and three 善's, and the pattern is chapter 66's: what arrives without being called.

## 繟然而善謀

繟: 帶緩也 — a sash tied loose.

So 繟然而善謀 is: like a belt tied slack, and nothing falls.

A tight belt leaves a mark and still lets the garment shift. A slack belt holds the same garment without pressing. The way of heaven's planning is that slack belt.

## 疏 is not sparse

疏: 通也 — open, passable. Not "few." The mesh is open so that air passes.

## 天網恢恢，疏而不失

恢恢 is the wide expanse.

Open and nothing lost.

通 and 不失 are opposites in ordinary logic: what lets things pass should let things escape. The chapter gives both.

So the net's principle is four words: it lets through, and it does not drop.

Which is the answer to 勇於敢: the way of heaven does not need to close its mesh. The one who closes it — tightening the belt, sealing every gap — has to keep holding it, and holding is what he will eventually lose.

## Why this follows 72

72 removed the display and the price.
73 removes the grip: the tight belt, the closed net, the 敢 that must keep taking.

And 疏而不失 is the description of what a life looks like when it is not holding.

## A test

Find the belt you have tied tight — the rule, the check, the escalation you keep in place. Ask whether it is tight because something slipped once, or because you cannot tolerate the slack. The second one is 敢.
